words.meaning: to cling as dust and mud do to shoes. Hence the orientals took off the sandals on entering a house.
words.plain: Cleaveth [Greek: kollethenta] — the word describes how dust and mud cling to sandals. Shaking it off was a deliberate, public gesture of separation: we've left your community entirely behind, and even the dust from your streets is no longer ours to carry.

words.meaning: Middle voice of an old verb apomassw, to rub off with the hands. Nowhere else in the N.T.
words.plain: We wipe off [Greek: apomassometha] means to rub something off with the hands — an emphatic, deliberate act. Combined with the dust imagery, it signals a complete break. The disciples aren't retreating; they're making a clear, public statement of rejection.
